properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 13 at 2:14PM MST until September 13 at 5:15PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Antelope Canyon in north central Arizona...

* Until 515 PM MST /615 PM MDT/.

* At 214 PM MST /314 PM MDT/, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms
producing heavy rain from Le Chee to Antelope Canyon. Flash
flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams and
normally dry washes.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Page, Lower Antelope Canyon, Owl Canyon, LeChee, Rattlesnake
Canyon, Mountain Sheep Canyon and Upper Antelope Canyon.

This includes the following slot canyons...
Lower Antelope Canyon, Owl Canyon and Rattlesnake Canyon.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Honey Draw and Antelope Creek.
properties.instruction:
Flooding of washes and creeks will occur, some dirt roads will become
muddy and impassable. Paved roads and underpasses could become
flooded as well.

CMAMtext: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 5:15 PM MST. Avoid flooded areas.
CMAMlongtext: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 5:15 PM MST. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

properties.description:

extending from Mount Herman to near Osyka to near Liberty, moving

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Expect damage to roofs, siding, and trees.

building.

flash flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded roadways.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 13 at 2:14PM MST until September 13 at 5:15PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Coconino County in north central Arizona...This includes the
Colorado River between river miles 113 and 154.

* Until 515 PM MST.

* At 214 PM MST, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across a large area of northwest Coconino County,
including several drainages in the Grand Canyon that flow into the
Colorado River. Between 0.75 and 1.5 inches of rain have fallen.
Additional rainfall amounts of 0.25 to 0.75 inches are possible in
the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams, and
normally dry washes.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Locust Point, Grand Canyon National Park, Alarcon Terrace, Tobar
Terrace, Blacktail Canyon, Garnet Canyon, Muav Canyon, Timp Point,
North Timp Point, Stina Point and Havasupai Reservation.

This includes the Colorado River between river miles 113 and 154.

This includes the following recreation areas and campgrounds...
Above Buckhorn Canyon Camp Site, 119.8 Mile Right Camp Site, 119.8
Mile Left Camp Site, Patch Camp Site, Upset Hotel Camp Site and
Sinyala Camp Site.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Hundred and Twentyseven Mile Creek, Hakatai Canyon, 119- Mile
Creek, 122- Mile Creek, Hundred and Twentyeight Mile Creek, 133-
Mile Creek, Galloway Canyon, Royal Arch Creek, Havasu Creek, Deer
Creek, Fossil Canyon, 128- Mile Creek, Fishtail Canyon, Blacktail
Canyon, Shinumo Creek, 140- Mile Canyon, Olo Canyon, Specter Chasm,
Stone Creek, Forster Canyon, Sinyella Canyon, Hundred and Twenty
Mile Creek, 150- Mile Canyon, Colorado River, "130- Mile Creek",
Matkatamiba Canyon, Tapeats Creek, Bonita Creek, 127-Mile Creek,
Garnet Canyon, "127.6- Mile Canyon", Waltenberg Canyon and Bedrock
Canyon.
properties.instruction:
Flooding of washes and creeks will occur, some dirt roads will become
muddy and impassable. Paved roads and underpasses could become
flooded as well.

Get out of washes and creeks if you are camping or hiking! Flooding
is occurring or imminent and will inundate creeks and washes.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 13 at 4:43PM MST until September 13 at 11:00PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Havasu Creek basin in...
Coconino County in north central Arizona...This includes the
Colorado River between river miles 156 and 158

* Until 1100 PM MST Sunday.

* At 443 PM MST, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain over portions of the Havasu Creek basin. Between 0.5 and
1.5 inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 0.25
to 0.75 inches are possible in the warned area. Runoff from these
storms will eventually flow into Havasu Creek and may cause flash
flooding through the evening hours.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the Havasu Creek basin.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Havasu Creek basin.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Little Navajo Falls, Mooney Falls, Beaver Falls, Hualapai Hilltop,
Havasupai Reservation and Supai.

This includes the Colorado River between river miles 156 and 158.

This includes the following swimming holes...
All swimming holes on Havasu Creek near Supai.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Little Coyote Canyon, Sinyella Canyon, Heather Wash, Pasture Wash,
Colorado River, Black Tank Wash and Havasu Creek.
properties.instruction:
Campers and hikers should hustle to higher ground immediately! Stay
away from creeks and washes!

Foot bridges will be washed out in Supai Campground. Some campsites
will be flooded. Campers may be stranded in portions of the
campground.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 13 at 6:03PM EDT until September 13 at 8:30PM EDT by NWS Pittsburgh PA
properties.description:
At 603 PM EDT, local law enforcement and doppler radar reported
thunderstorms producing heavy rain across the warned area. Between
1.5 and 2 inches of rain have fallen. Flash flooding is ongoing or
expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Law enforcement reported.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Hermitage, Sharon, Sharpsville, Farrell and Wheatland.

Roads were flooded near Farrell.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 13 at 7:09PM EDT until September 14 at 2:00AM EDT by NWS Boston/Norton MA
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Norton has issued a Flood Warning
for the following rivers in Rhode Island...

Pawtuxet River At Cranston affecting Kent and Providence Counties.

For the Pawtuxet River...including Cranston, Scituate Reservoir...
Minor flooding is forecast.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued late tonight at 200 AM EDT.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Pawtuxet River at Cranston.

* WHEN...From this evening to late tonight.

* IMPACTS...At 9.0 feet, Minor lowland flooding will occur along the
river as it flows through Warwick and Cranston.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 6:45 PM EDT Sunday the stage was 9.0 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 9.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 9.1 feet
this evening. It will then fall below flood stage just after
midnight tonight.
- Flood stage is 9.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 9.1
feet on 11/06/1955.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
